description: Ask about preparation, film, and the boring repetition rather than the highlight. Career-length anxiety and the business side are real and under-covered; a defining public failure is not something to spring on someone.

questions.text: What does the work look like on a Tuesday in the off-season?
questions.lands_because: Moves straight past the game to the repetition that actually constitutes the profession, which is what athletes and coaches mostly do and rarely get asked about.
followups: What is the most tedious part that matters most?

questions.text: What do you see on film that a knowledgeable fan watching the same play would miss?
questions.lands_because: Specifying a knowledgeable fan raises the bar and produces genuine technical detail rather than a generic answer about hard work.
followups: Teach me what to look for next time I watch.

questions.text: How do you manage knowing the career has a fixed end?
questions.lands_because: Career brevity shapes everything - money, injury decisions, identity - and athletes think about it constantly while mostly being asked about the next game.
followups: What are you building for after?

questions.text: What is the injury decision you have made that you would make differently now?
questions.lands_because: Playing through injury sits at the intersection of pressure, money, and medical advice. It is honest and concrete without requiring the guest to blame anyone.
followups: Who was in your ear at the time?
questions.avoid_if: The guest is currently in a contract negotiation or dealing with an active injury.

questions.text: What does the locker room know about a teammate that the coaching staff does not?
questions.lands_because: Information asymmetry inside a team is real and fascinating, and it can be answered in general terms without betraying anyone.

questions.text: What do you understand about the business of this sport now that you did not at the start?
questions.lands_because: Contracts, agents, media obligations, and revenue structures are a genuine education athletes acquire the hard way, and it moves the interview off the field.
followups: What do you tell younger players about it?
